# Novu

## What This Is
Novu is communication infrastructure for products and agents across Inbox, email, SMS, push and chat channels.

## Non-Negotiables
- Work in active apps `api`, `dashboard`, `worker`, `ws`; reuse shared packages. Business work follows `libs/application-generic`; persistence follows `libs/dal` repositories.
- Ask before adding dependencies, changing MongoDB/ClickHouse schemas, editing `enterprise/` or `packages/providers/`, or creating UI components outside dashboard `src/components/`.
- Never hand-edit `libs/internal-sdk`; leave inactive `apps/webhook` alone except necessary monorepo refactors. Reuse existing Radix/shadcn UI; do not copy playground patterns.
- Preserve CE, Cloud and on-prem EE boundaries. Gate Enterprise and Cloud changes for their supported distributions.
- Use `NODE_ENV=test` for API/worker/ws tests. This checkout is prepared; do not rerun `pnpm setup:agent`. READ BROAD, GROUND TIGHT: verify claims in code and ground each to the few implementing symbols.

## Commands
- Dev: `pnpm start:api:dev`, `pnpm start:dashboard`, `pnpm start:worker`, `pnpm start:ws` (reuse running services).
- Tests: `pnpm --filter @novu/api-service test`; `pnpm --filter @novu/dashboard test:e2e`.
- Lint: `pnpm lint`; targeted: `pnpm --filter @novu/api-service check`.
- Build: `pnpm build` after package/Enterprise changes; app-only edits need no monorepo rebuild. See `context/setup.md` for library rebuild guidance.

## Project Knowledge
For a question about project decisions, conventions, or behavior, start with `mex wiki query "<question>" --limit 5 --json`. Inspect matched terms and each grounding's health: partial matches are leads, and `changed` means re-check the claim against code. If the index is unavailable, follow `ROUTER.md` or start from `mex graph scope "<task>"`. Reads never rebuild or refresh an index.

## Code Graph
Use the smallest relevant structured resolver. For Inbox or Relay mutations, resolve only the intended action with `mex inbox contract --action <command-id> --json` or `mex relay contract --action <command-id> --json`; use `mex capabilities --json` only for broader capability discovery. If the user explicitly asks to create, save, or draft a checkout-local Inbox or Relay draft, preview and apply that exact draft without asking for redundant confirmation. Deleting a local draft, or publishing, approving, rejecting, withdrawing, marking stale, repairing, taking or acknowledging, or closing, requires fresh explicit confirmation after semantic preview. Treat Git commit, push, and pull as separate actions requiring their own authorization.

The repo is indexed into `.mex/graph.db`. Use it to avoid re-reading code you already have — it is one tool alongside Grep/Glob, not a replacement for them.
- If you know the symbol name, go straight to it: `mex graph query <who-calls|what-calls|where-defined> <symbol>` and `mex graph get <id...>` are exact. This is the strongest part of the graph. Each call first proves the whole index is still fresh, so on a large repository it takes seconds: pass several ids to one `graph get` instead of calling it once per id. Give it exact names — an approximate name can return a confident wrong match.
- Exploring an unfamiliar task? `mex graph scope "<task>"` returns bounded, source-backed JSONL context plus trustworthy execution flows. Scope matches on words, not meaning, so treat it as starting evidence rather than a complete answer.
- Treat source returned by the graph as ALREADY READ; do not re-open those files.
- Read the summary status and evidence. `status: "ok"` remains usable when `truncated: true`; only optional evidence was omitted. For `partial` or `degraded`, narrow the task or follow `suggestedNextCommands`.
- Use `mex graph get <id> --detail source` only when source is missing, you need exact expansion, or a partial/degraded summary suggests it. Do not expand nodes by quota.
- If the evidence is insufficient or the task wording does not match the code, use Grep/Glob instead. Do not re-run `scope` with reworded phrasing more than once.
- Before editing a symbol, run `mex impact <symbol|file>` to see affected callers and scaffold memory.
- During `mex sync`, adjudicate any AMBIGUOUS grounding; after repairs, ensure the refreshed grounding is re-emitted.

## Scaffold Growth
After meaningful work, run GROW:
- Ground: what changed in reality?
- Record: update `ROUTER.md` and relevant `context/` files
- Connect: keep each section linked to its enclosing knowledge with `refines`; preview missing structural links with `mex wiki link-sections`, then apply explicitly. Add semantic relationships only with evidence; backlinks are derived.
- Orient: create or update a `patterns/` runbook if this can recur
- Write: bump `last_updated` on changed scaffold files; optional `mex log` notes follow the logging policy below

## Agent Logging
Read `mex logging --json` at session start and before optional logging. This checkout-local advisory preference is `significant` (quiet default: material decisions, risks, blockers, or durable discoveries), `checkpoints` (batch useful notes at task/session boundaries), or `manual` (no unsolicited notes). Skip routine tool calls, edits, repeated status, and empty summaries. Honor explicit user log requests in every mode; never suppress mandatory workflow Activity or recovery audit records. Report a policy read failure instead of guessing or changing the preference.

When earlier work may inform the task, use `mex timeline --query "subject phrase" --file src/example.ts --limit 10 --json` with a known subject or exact recorded file path, or both. These are historical notes, not accepted current knowledge. Verify conclusions before reuse or explicit promotion with their source retained.

The scaffold grows from real work, not just setup. See the GROW step in `ROUTER.md` for details.

## Navigation
At the start of every session, read `ROUTER.md` before doing anything else.
For full project context, patterns, and task guidance — everything is there.

<!-- mex-agent:skills:start -->
## MEX context policy
- When MEX context materially helps your work, mention MEX and the relevant finding naturally in your explanation. Tie the mention to what it helped you understand, decide, or verify. Avoid fixed phrases, standalone acknowledgements, repeated mentions, or narrating routine context loading. This replaces older MEX instructions requiring a fixed acknowledgement or context-loading narration.
- Do not claim an author, date, or historical event unless the retrieved data actually provides it.
- After a MEX write, say exactly what changed and its sharing boundary: a local draft is checkout-only and nothing is shared; a canonical artifact is written to the working tree and requires commit/push to share.
- Skill activation is not approval for canonical actions.
<!-- mex-agent:skills:end -->

# Session Bootstrap

If you haven't already read `AGENTS.md`, read it now — it contains the project identity, non-negotiables, and commands.

Then read this file fully before doing anything else in this session.

## Current Project State
**Working (implementation present; no runtime validation performed in this documentation session):**
- NestJS API with versioned feature modules, authentication, validation and OpenAPI tooling.
- React dashboard with workflow, integration, subscriber, activity and agent routes.
- Background notification execution and Socket.io real-time delivery applications.
- pnpm/Nx workspace, app-specific tests and prepared agent environment as supplied by session instructions.

**Not yet built / intentionally unavailable:**
- LLM Gateway controller wiring is parked in `enterpriseImports()` in `apps/api/src/app.module.ts`.
- Enterprise implementation is supplied separately through `.source`; it is not part of a standalone CE checkout.
- [TO DETERMINE] No authoritative unimplemented-feature backlog was provided; inspect the relevant spec/ticket before treating a feature as absent.

**Known issues and constraints:**
- API Mocha's default setup drops the configured MongoDB database; require `NODE_ENV=test` and isolate unit specs with `--no-config` when appropriate.
- API bootstrap documents an instrumented double-parse failure; preserve manual parser ownership.
- pnpm release-age and CodeMirror peer-instance workarounds are documented in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; preserve them during dependency changes.

## Routing Table

Load the relevant file based on the current task. Always load `context/architecture.md` first if not already in context this session.

| Task type | Load |
|-----------|------|
| Understanding how the system works | `context/architecture.md` |
| Working with a specific technology | `context/stack.md` |
| Writing or reviewing code | `context/conventions.md` |
| Making a design decision | `context/decisions.md` |
| Setting up or running the project | `context/setup.md` |
| Any specific task | Check `patterns/INDEX.md` for a matching pattern |

## Behavioural Contract

For every task, follow this loop:

1. **CONTEXT** — Load the relevant context file(s) from the routing table above. Check `patterns/INDEX.md` for a matching pattern. If one exists, follow it.
2. **BUILD** — Do the work. If a pattern exists, follow its Steps. If you are about to deviate from an established pattern, say so before writing any code — state the deviation and why.
3. **VERIFY** — Load `context/conventions.md` and run the Verify Checklist item by item. State each item and whether the output passes. Do not summarise — enumerate explicitly.
4. **DEBUG** — If verification fails or something breaks, check `patterns/INDEX.md` for a debug pattern. Follow it. Fix the issue and re-run VERIFY.
5. **GROW** — After meaningful work, run this binary checklist:
   - **Ground:** What changed in reality? Name the changed behavior, system, command, dependency, or workflow.
   - **Record:** If project state changed, update the "Current Project State" section above. If documented facts changed, update the relevant `context/` file surgically. Record a new behavioral claim about specific code as its own entity (`mex wiki apply` with a `create-entry` operation), grounded to every symbol whose change could make it false and naming the identifiers and literals it depends on. Ground with node ids only; MEX records the fingerprints. Give the entity 3 to 6 `aliases` (short plain-word phrases a developer would type for the symptom or outcome it covers, written from the claim itself, not its title or identifiers).
   - **Connect:** Link section entities to their enclosing knowledge with `refines` using existing ids. Preview missing structural links with `mex wiki link-sections`, then apply explicitly. Review semantic relationships from evidence; do not connect records just because they share keywords or code groundings.
   - **Orient:** If this task can recur and no pattern exists, create one in `patterns/` using `patterns/README.md`, then add it to `patterns/INDEX.md`. If a pattern exists but you learned a gotcha, update it.
   - **Write:** Bump `last_updated` in every scaffold file you changed. Read `mex logging --json` before optional `mex log` notes: `significant` records material rationale, `checkpoints` batches useful notes at task/session boundaries, and `manual` avoids unsolicited notes. Honor explicit user log requests in every mode; mandatory workflow Activity and recovery audits remain required.

# Setup — Populate This Scaffold

This file contains the prompts to populate the scaffold. It is NOT the dev environment setup — for that, see `context/setup.md` after population.

This scaffold is currently empty. Follow the steps below to populate it for your project.

## Recommended: Use `mex setup`

```bash
mex setup
```

This opens the terminal setup HUD. Highlight your AI tool and press Enter to
select it and start; Space optionally selects additional integrations. Use
`mex setup --browser` for browser setup, or `mex setup --dry-run` for a read-only
terminal preview. `--cli` remains an alias for the default terminal flow.

Setup runs the following steps, then opens the Hub for review and completion:
1. Detects your project state without overwriting existing scaffold files
2. Protects `.mex/graph.db*`, `.mex/wiki.db*`, and `.mex/local/` from Git
3. Installs the project instructions for your selected AI tools
4. Scans the codebase and builds the local code graph
5. Hands the terminal to the first selected available Claude Code or Codex CLI; exiting the agent returns to MEX for file checks, with a manual prompt when population is incomplete (browser setup uses a background agent session)
6. Captures grounding, migrates the populated Markdown, builds the Wiki index, and validates it
7. Shows the exact setup diff for an explicit local commit, with a manual Git option
8. Shows a completion guide, optional global install at the running version, and optional contact details before **Open Hub**

Global install and contact submission are optional. Email is needed only if you
choose to send contact details; name is optional. Contact details go through the
embedded form service and stay out of project files and usage telemetry.
The introductory Hub tour begins after opening the full Hub.

For scripts, use `--yes` and repeatable `--tool` flags (or `--tool none`).
Piped input/output and CI also use plain output and never launch an agent or
long-lived Hub. Exit 2 means population is pending; populate the scaffold and
rerun setup to continue. Exit 0 means preparation is complete. Use
`mex setup --browser` to open the commit and completion page afterward.

For Claude Code and Codex, setup also copies the packaged `mex-inbox` and
`mex-relay` skills into the project. No plugin or separate skill installer is
needed. A plain `npm install` delivers the payload without changing the
repository; after upgrading the package, run `mex skills sync` to install the
new packaged copies for the tools recorded in `.mex/config.json`.

If you want to populate manually instead, use the prompts below.

## Detecting Your State

**Existing codebase?** Follow Option A.
**Fresh project, nothing built yet?** Follow Option B.
**Partially built?** Follow Option A — the agent will flag empty slots it cannot fill yet.

---

## Option A — Existing Codebase

Paste the following prompt into your agent:

---

**SETUP PROMPT — copy everything between the lines:**

```
You are going to populate an AI context scaffold for this project.
The scaffold lives in the root of this repository.

Read the following files in order before doing anything else:
1. ROUTER.md — understand the scaffold structure
2. context/architecture.md — read the annotation comments to understand what belongs there
3. context/stack.md — same
4. context/conventions.md — same
5. context/decisions.md — same
6. context/setup.md — same

Then explore this codebase:
- Read the main entry point(s)
- Read the folder structure
- Read 2-3 representative files from each major layer
- Read any existing README or documentation

PASS 1 — Populate knowledge files:

Populate each context/ file by replacing the annotation comments
with real content from this codebase. Follow the annotation instructions exactly.
For each slot:
- Use the actual names, patterns, and structures from this codebase
- Do not use generic examples
- Do not leave any slot empty — if you cannot determine the answer,
  write "[TO DETERMINE]" and explain what information is needed
- Keep length within the guidance given in each annotation

Then assess: does this project have domains complex enough that cramming
them into architecture.md would make it too long or too shallow?
If yes, create additional domain-specific context files in context/.
Examples: a project with a complex auth system gets context/auth.md.
A data pipeline gets context/ingestion.md. A project with Stripe gets
context/payments.md. Use the same YAML frontmatter format (name,
description, triggers, edges, last_updated), plus a `type` key that
says what the file is so the Wiki indexes it: `type: component` for a
subsystem or domain (the usual case), `type: guide` for a runbook, or
`type: convention` for rules. Only create these for domains that have real depth — not for simple
integrations that fit in a few lines of architecture.md.

After populating context/ files, update ROUTER.md:
- Fill in the Current Project State section based on what you found
- Add rows to the routing table for any domain-specific context files you created

Update AGENTS.md:
- Fill in the project name, one-line description, non-negotiables, and commands

PASS 2 — Generate starter patterns:

Read patterns/README.md for the format and categories.

Generate 3-5 starter patterns for the most common and most dangerous task
types in this project. Focus on:
- The 1-2 tasks a developer does most often (e.g., add endpoint, add component)
- The 1-2 integrations with the most non-obvious gotchas
- 1 debug pattern for the most common failure boundary

Each pattern should be specific to this project — real file paths, real gotchas,
real verify steps derived from the code you read in Pass 1.
Use the format in patterns/README.md. Name descriptively (e.g., add-endpoint.md).

Do NOT try to generate a pattern for every possible task type. The scaffold
grows incrementally — the behavioural contract (step 5: GROW) will create
new patterns from real work as the project evolves. Setup just seeds the most
critical ones.

After generating patterns, update patterns/INDEX.md with a row for each
pattern file you created. For multi-section patterns, add one row per task
section using anchor links (see INDEX.md annotation for format).

PASS 3 — Wire the web:

Setup links each fact to its file for you, so do not wire section links by
hand. Add cross-entity relationships only when the content gives evidence for
them; never invent links to meet a count or duplicate inverse backlinks.

Re-read every file you just wrote (context/ files, pattern files, ROUTER.md).
For each file, add or update the `edges` array in the YAML frontmatter.
Each edge should point to another scaffold file that is meaningfully related,
with a `condition` explaining when an agent should follow that edge.

Rules for edges:
- Add only meaningful edges supported by the content; there is no minimum count
- Link a pattern to its relevant context file when the content supports it
- Edges should be bidirectional where it makes sense (if A links to B, consider B linking to A)
- Use relative paths (e.g., context/stack.md, patterns/add-endpoint.md)
- Pattern files can edge to other patterns (e.g., debug pattern → related task pattern)

Important: only write content derived from the codebase.
Do not include system-injected text (dates, reminders, etc.)
in any scaffold file.

When done, confirm which files were populated and flag any slots
you could not fill with confidence.
```

---

## Option B — Fresh Project

Paste the following prompt into your agent:

---

**SETUP PROMPT — copy everything between the lines:**

```
You are going to populate an AI context scaffold for a project that
is just starting. Nothing is built yet.

Read the following files in order before doing anything else:
1. ROUTER.md — understand the scaffold structure
2. All files in context/ — read the annotation comments in each

Then ask me the following questions one section at a time.
Wait for my answer before moving to the next section:

1. What does this project do? (one sentence)
2. What are the hard rules — things that must never happen in this codebase?
3. What is the tech stack? (language, framework, database, key libraries)
4. Why did you choose this stack over alternatives?
5. How will the major pieces connect? Describe the flow of a typical request/action.
6. What patterns do you want to enforce from day one?
7. What are you deliberately NOT building or using?

After I answer, populate the context/ files based on my answers.
For any slot you cannot fill yet, write "[TO BE DETERMINED]" and note
what needs to be decided before it can be filled.

Then assess: based on my answers, does this project have domains complex
enough that cramming them into architecture.md would make it too long
or too shallow? If yes, create additional domain-specific context files
in context/. Examples: a project with a complex auth system gets
context/auth.md. A data pipeline gets context/ingestion.md. A project
with Stripe gets context/payments.md. Use the same YAML frontmatter
format (name, description, triggers, edges, last_updated), plus a
`type` key that says what the file is so the Wiki indexes it:
`type: component` for a subsystem or domain (the usual case),
`type: guide` for a runbook, or `type: convention` for rules. Only create
these for domains that have real depth — not for simple integrations
that fit in a few lines of architecture.md. For fresh projects, mark
domain-specific unknowns with "[TO BE DETERMINED — populate after first
implementation]".

Update ROUTER.md current state to reflect that this is a new project.
Add rows to the routing table for any domain-specific context files you created.
Update AGENTS.md with the project name, description, non-negotiables, and commands.

Read patterns/README.md for the format and categories.

Generate 2-3 starter patterns for the most obvious task types you can
anticipate for this stack. Focus on the tasks a developer will do first.
Mark unknowns with "[VERIFY AFTER FIRST IMPLEMENTATION]".

Do NOT try to anticipate every possible pattern. The scaffold grows
incrementally — the behavioural contract (step 5: GROW) will create
new patterns from real work as the project evolves. Setup just seeds
the most critical ones.

After generating patterns, update patterns/INDEX.md with a row for each
pattern file you created.

PASS 3 — Wire the web:

Setup links each fact to its file for you, so do not wire section links by
hand. Semantic dependencies need evidence, not link quotas.

Re-read every file you just wrote (context/ files, pattern files, ROUTER.md).
For each file, add or update the `edges` array in the YAML frontmatter.
Each edge should point to another scaffold file that is meaningfully related,
with a `condition` explaining when an agent should follow that edge.

Rules for edges:
- Add only meaningful edges supported by the content; there is no minimum count
- Link a pattern to its relevant context file when the content supports it
- Edges should be bidirectional where it makes sense
- Use relative paths (e.g., context/stack.md, patterns/add-endpoint.md)

Important: only write content derived from your answers.
Do not include system-injected text (dates, reminders, etc.)
in any scaffold file.
```

---

## After Setup

Start a new Claude Code or Codex session so the new project skills and
instructions are guaranteed to load. Claude uses `/mex-inbox` and `/mex-relay`;
Codex uses `$mex-inbox` and `$mex-relay`. Clear natural-language requests work
too. Commit the project skill copies so teammates receive them; MEX never
stages, commits, or pushes them automatically.

Setup prints the scoped Git commands for the selected tools. Review those files
and commit them before running `mex hub`; Hub requires `.mex/config.json` to
match the version committed at the current Git `HEAD`. The local Graph/Wiki
databases and `.mex/local/` remain ignored.

**Verify** by starting a fresh session and asking your agent:
"Read `.mex/ROUTER.md` and tell me what you now know about this project."

A well-populated scaffold should give the agent enough to:
- Describe the architecture without looking at code
- Name the non-negotiable conventions
- Know which files to load for any given task type
- Know which patterns exist for common task types

## Keeping It Fresh

Once the scaffold is populated, use these to keep it aligned with your codebase:

- **`mex check`** — detect drift (zero tokens, zero AI)
- **`mex sync`** — interactive drift check + targeted resync
- **`mex skills sync`** — safely receive updated official agent skills after a package upgrade
- **`mex watch`** — auto drift score after every commit

# Sync — Realign This Scaffold

## Recommended: Use `mex sync`

```bash
mex sync
```

The command runs drift detection first, shows you exactly what's wrong, then offers:
1. **Targeted sync** — AI fixes only the flagged files (fastest, cheapest)
2. **Full resync** — AI re-reads everything and updates all scaffold files
3. **Prompt export** — shows the prompts for manual paste
4. **Exit** — fix it yourself

In the same session the agent reviews each Wiki entity whose linked code changed:
still true → `mex wiki reground <id> --apply`; changed → fix the text, then reground;
unsure → leave the flag. Sync then rebuilds the Wiki index and checks again.

## Quick Check

```bash
mex check              # full drift report, including Wiki code links
mex check --quiet      # one-liner: "drift score 85/100 (1 error)"
mex sync --dry-run     # preview targeted fix prompts
```

## Manual Resync

If you prefer to paste a prompt manually, or don't have the CLI built:

---

**SYNC PROMPT — copy everything between the lines:**

```
You are going to resync the AI context scaffold for this project.
The scaffold may be out of date — the codebase has changed since it was last populated.

First, read all files in context/ to understand the current scaffold state.
Then explore what has changed in the codebase since the scaffold was last updated.
Check the last_updated dates in the YAML frontmatter of each file.

For each context/ file:
1. Compare the current scaffold content to the actual codebase
2. Identify what has changed, been added, or been removed
3. Update the file to reflect the current state

Critical rules for updating:
- Use surgical, targeted edits — NOT full file rewrites. Read the existing content,
  identify what changed, and update only those sections.
- PRESERVE YAML frontmatter structure. Never delete or rewrite the entire frontmatter block.
  Edit individual fields only. The edges, triggers, name, and description fields must
  survive every sync. If you need to update edges, add or remove individual entries —
  do not replace the entire array.
- In context/decisions.md: NEVER delete existing decisions.
  If a decision has changed, mark the old entry as "Superseded by [new decision title]"
  and add the new decision above it with today's date.
- In all other files: update content to reflect current reality
- Update last_updated in the YAML frontmatter of every file you change
- After updating each file, update ROUTER.md Current Project State

When done, report:
- Which files were updated and what changed
- Any decisions that were superseded
- Any slots that could not be filled with confidence
```

## Agents API

`AgentsModule` assembles agent management, channel integrations, conversation ingress and replies, managed runtime execution, subscriber Agent Chat, email actions, and MCP connectivity. Main HTTP entry points include `AgentsController`, `AgentInboundController`, `AgentReplyController`, and `AgentChatController`. Controllers and use-cases connect dashboard and SDK requests to DAL repositories, shared application services, platform adapters, customer bridges, and managed runtime providers.

## Failed managed provisioning compensates for absent transactions

`CreateAgent.execute()` inserts a managed agent inside `agentRepository.withTransaction()` before calling `ProvisionManagedAgent.execute()`. If provisioning or subsequent adoption handling throws and the callback has no `session`, it explicitly deletes the just-created agent using its ID, environment, and organization, then rethrows. This compensating delete covers local deployments without a replica-set transaction; with a session, the error is left to abort the transaction.

## Production agent updates permit only active status and the main bridge URL

`UpdateAgent.execute()` sends name, description, or any recognized behavior change through `assertNotProduction()`, and separately rejects changes to `devBridgeUrl` or `devBridgeActive` there. `assertNotProduction()` throws `ForbiddenException` only when the scoped environment has `type === EnvironmentTypeEnum.PROD`. Changes to `active` and `bridgeUrl` do not take this production-rejection path.

## Deleting an agent preserves its provider agent unless explicitly requested

`DeleteAgent.execute()` calls `deleteFromProvider()` only for a managed agent with `managedRuntime` and `command.deleteFromProvider === true`, before local transactional cleanup. `deleteFromProvider()` always skips `AgentRuntimeProviderIdEnum.NovuAnthropic` to avoid cross-tenant deletion on the shared demo account; it also returns when the integration or resolved runtime is unavailable. An actual provider deletion error propagates before local cleanup.

## Moving a demo agent to an owned key starts new provider sessions

`MigrateAgentRuntime.execute()` accepts a managed agent on the `NovuAnthropic` demo integration and an active `IntegrationKindEnum.AGENT` target using `Anthropic`, with a resolved API key and `externalEnvironmentId`. It copies provider configuration into a newly created agent, updates `managedRuntime`, and calls `clearExternalSessionIdsForAgent()` in the transaction. If that transaction fails, it attempts to delete the newly created target agent and rethrows.

## Inbound link healing cannot resurrect a deliberate disconnection

When `AgentConfigResolver.resolve()` finds no live agent-integration link, it explicitly queries `disconnectedAt: { $ne: null }` and throws `AgentIntegrationDisconnectedException` for a tombstone before attempting healing. `tryHealMissingAgentIntegrationLink()` only attempts auto-linking for `source === 'webhook_message'` and refuses an integration already linked to another agent. Verification handshakes and outbound resolutions do not create missing links.

## Inactive and disconnected webhooks receive a successful empty acknowledgment

`AgentInboundController.routeWebhook()` catches `AgentInactiveException` and `AgentIntegrationDisconnectedException` and sends HTTP `200` with `{}` to avoid provider retries. Other `HttpException` instances retain their own status and response body; non-HTTP errors are rethrown. A successful webhook acknowledgment therefore does not prove the event reached an agent runtime.

## An active development bridge overrides the context and agent endpoints

`BridgeExecutorService.resolveBridgeUrl()` chooses `devBridgeUrl` when both `devBridgeActive` and `devBridgeUrl` are truthy, otherwise `bridgeUrlOverride`, otherwise `config.bridgeUrl`. It returns `null` if none is available. On the selected URL it sets query parameters `action=agent-event`, `agentId` to the agent identifier, and `event` to the dispatched event, replacing existing values of those keys.

## Changing the first managed vault discards the existing runtime session

`ManagedAgentService.reconcileSessionIdForVaultBinding()` compares `conversation.managedSessionVaultId` with `vaultIds[0]` when an `existingSessionId` exists. A mismatch clears the stored external session and returns `undefined`; a match preserves the session. `dispatch()` uses that returned value for `provider.send()` and chooses history-based messages when it is absent. The code documents that the provider applies vault IDs only when creating a session.

## Per-tool trust overrides the source-wide default

`ToolTrustService.isToolTrusted()` selects `trust.mcp[tool.mcpServerName]` for an MCP tool and the shared `trust.direct` entry for other tools. It resolves policy in the order `tools[tool.toolName] ?? serverDefault ?? DEFAULT_TOOL_TRUST_POLICY`, and returns true only for the literal `always_allow`. An explicit per-tool policy therefore takes precedence over an allow rule on the whole server or direct-tool source.

## Bulk MCP changes enable first and report per-row failures

`SetAgentMcpServers.execute()` invokes `assertAllIdsInCatalog()` before any enable/disable mutation, so unknown IDs reject the request up front. It then sequentially enables requested additions before disabling removals, catches each mutation failure into `failed`, and continues. Finally it re-reads with `enabledOnly: true` and returns that state alongside the failures; a completed bulk call can therefore contain both successful and unsuccessful mutations.

## Agent Chat POST verification requires an Inbox subscriber token

`AgentChatSessionVerifier.verifySession()` requires a Bearer authorization header, a nonempty token, and `JWT_SECRET`. ## Agent event batches must have one conversation and one agent identity

## Text approval interception runs before unresolved-subscriber access replies

In `AgentInboundHandler.handle()`, after the inbound message is recorded and the turn is built, an `ON_MESSAGE` turn is passed to `replyApprovalInterceptor.tryHandleAsApprovalReply()` before `maybeReplyUnresolvedSubscriberAccess()`. A true result returns immediately, skipping both that access reply and the normal `runtime.dispatch(turn)` call. This ordering lets a pending approval reply be consumed without also dispatching its original message as a new turn.

## API shared infrastructure

`apps/api/src/app/shared/` supplies cross-feature API infrastructure: `SharedModule` composes DAL repositories, application-generic services, logging and queues; framework interceptors and Swagger helpers shape HTTP contracts; shared commands, DTOs, validators and auth helpers support feature controllers and use-cases. `SingleUseTokenCache` is reused by Connect, Telegram mobile linking and WhatsApp signup-link services. HTML and URL helpers support browser connection flows.

## Response wrapping uses truthy data and identity fields

`ResponseInterceptor.intercept()` bypasses wrapping for `graphql`. Otherwise, `returnWholeObject()` preserves the outer response fields only when `data?.data` is truthy and neither `data?._id` nor `data?.id` is truthy. Every other result is placed under a new `data` property. Thus an entity with a truthy `id` and its own `data` field receives an outer wrapper, while a result with a falsy `data` field does not qualify as an existing wrapper.

## Idempotency keys share an organization-wide namespace

`IdempotencyInterceptor.getCacheKey()` builds `${env}-${user.organizationId}-${this.getIdempotencyKey(context)}`, where `env` is `process.env.NODE_ENV`, `getReqUser()` reads `req.user`, and `getIdempotencyKey()` reads the lowercased `HttpResponseHeaderKeysEnum.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` header. The cache key contains no environment ID, user ID, HTTP method or route, so reusing a header value across those boundaries within the same organization and NODE_ENV addresses the same cache entry. An undefined user causes `InternalServerErrorException` before a key can be built.

## API-key and keyless credentials cannot override environment scope

`assertEnvironmentScopedAccess()` applies its environment restriction only when `isEnvironmentScopedAuthScheme()` identifies `ApiAuthSchemeEnum.API_KEY` or `ApiAuthSchemeEnum.KEYLESS`. For those schemes, a truthy `requestedEnvironmentId` differing from `userEnvironmentId` throws `ForbiddenException`; an omitted or empty target, a matching target, and other authentication schemes return without throwing. This helper validates a target; it does not fill in a missing environment ID.

## Self-hosted custom domains bypass the service-level lookup

For a route requesting `ProductFeatureKeyEnum.CUSTOM_DOMAINS`, `ProductFeatureInterceptor.intercept()` calls `next.handle()` before `organizationRepository.findById()` and the service-level check when `process.env.IS_SELF_HOSTED === 'true'`. The `getReqUser()` check still happens first, so a missing `req.user` throws `UnauthorizedException` even on this bypass. The exception is specific to `CUSTOM_DOMAINS` and the literal string `'true'`.

## Token release uses the original remaining lifetime

`SingleUseTokenCache.release()` silently returns when `isValidTokenFormat(token)` fails, `cacheEnabled()` is false, or `entry.expiresAt - Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) <= 0`. For an eligible entry it preserves `entry.expiresAt` and passes that remaining number of seconds to `cacheService.eval()`, rather than granting a fresh `ttlSeconds` lifetime. Retrying release therefore cannot revive an already expired entry through this method.

## API-key OpenAPI filtering leaves unspecified security untouched

`removeEndpointsWithoutApiKey()` examines only operations with a truthy `operation.security`. Within those arrays it keeps entries containing `API_KEY_SWAGGER_SECURITY_NAME` and removes the operation if none match; an explicit empty `security: []` therefore removes the operation, while an absent `security` property leaves it untouched. This is an operation-level filter, not a computation of inherited document security.

## Shared backend application services

`libs/application-generic` is the `@novu/application-generic` backend library used by the API, worker, and WebSocket applications. Its `src/index.ts` entry point exposes shared commands, DTOs, use cases, services, modules, factories, and utilities. Notification orchestration lives under `src/usecases/`, including triggering, subscriber and tenant processing, preference merging, integration selection, and template execution. `src/services/` supplies queue backends, cache and feature-flag adapters, analytics logging, and payload/template hydration; `QueuesModule.forRoot()` supplies queue-related Nest providers. Persistence is delegated to `@novu/dal` repositories, shared contracts come from `@novu/shared`, and bridge execution connects to the framework and step-resolver paths.

## Trigger transaction reuse is rejected per environment

`TriggerEvent.execute()` calls `validateTransactionIdProperty(transactionId, environmentId)` before dispatching to broadcast or multicast. The validator searches jobs using exactly `transactionId` and `_environmentId`, projecting `_id`; finding any job throws `BadRequestException` with the message beginning `transactionId property is not unique`. This is a rejection of an already-used transaction, rather than an idempotent success response; the check is scoped to an environment and does not filter by workflow identifier.

## Topic exclusions are unioned before expansion

`splitByRecipientType()` collects explicit subscribers in `singleSubscribers` and exclusions by topic key in `topicExclusions`. `TriggerMulticast.execute()` sends explicit subscribers first, then flattens all topic exclusion sets into `allTopicExcludedSubscribers` and passes their union, together with `singleSubscriberIds`, as `excludeSubscribers` to the single `getTopicDistinctSubscribers()` query for all requested topic ids. An exclusion attached to one topic therefore contributes to the exclusion query for every requested topic; it does not remove an explicitly addressed subscriber from the earlier explicit-recipient batch.

## Explicit integration identifiers bypass tenant overrides

`SelectIntegration.execute()` starts with the fallback from `getPrimaryIntegration()`. It attempts tenant-conditioned overrides only when `!command.identifier && command.filterData.tenant && command.userId`. In that branch it skips integrations without conditions, normalizes variables containing the resolved `tenant`, evaluates `conditionsFilter.filter()`, and replaces the fallback with the first candidate whose `passed` result is true, then breaks. Supplying `identifier` bypasses that entire override loop; with no passing candidate, the original fallback remains.

## Hidden integration credentials remain an empty object

When `command.returnCredentials === false`, `GetDecryptedIntegrations.execute()` returns each integration with `credentials: {}` and does not call `getDecryptedCredentials()` for that item. It preserves the required object field rather than omitting it: the source explicitly cites compatibility with older `@novu/api` SDK zod schemas, including version `3.15.0`, that reject an absent `credentials` object.

## Read-only workflow settings suppress subscriber merge layers

`MergePreferences.execute()` applies `toMerged()` in the order `workflowResourcePreference`, `workflowUserPreference`, `subscriberGlobalPreference`, then `subscriberWorkflowPreference`, so later included layers override earlier ones. If any workflow layer has `preferences.all?.readOnly`, or `excludeSubscriberPreferences` is true, both subscriber layers are excluded from the merge. The returned `source` still includes the original subscriber preference objects even when they were excluded from the effective result.

## Disabling subscriber updates still permits creation

After resolving the existing subscriber, `CreateOrUpdateSubscriberUseCase.execute()` checks `failIfExists` first and throws `ConflictException` if the subscriber exists. Otherwise `allowUpdate` controls updating an existing subscriber and the separate channel-credential update: `command.channels?.length && command.allowUpdate` is required for `updateCredentials()`. With `allowUpdate` false, an existing subscriber is returned directly, but an absent subscriber still takes the `createSubscriber()` branch. Treat `allowUpdate` as an update switch, not an existing-subscriber requirement.

## Existing payloads take precedence during batch hydration

`NotificationPayloadService.fetchNotificationPayloads()` fetches only carriers with `payload == null` and a `_notificationId`, deduplicating notification ids separately for each `_environmentId` and querying `_id payload` once per environment. `hydrateEntitiesPayload()` mutates only those missing payloads in place. Any non-null payload, including `{}`, is already complete and is neither fetched nor merged with notification data.

## Lean job templates use live, direct, then deleted lookups

`StepTemplateHydrationService.hydrateJobStep()` skips full snapshots detected by `isLeanStepTemplate()` through `template._environmentId`, and skips jobs with no workflow `_templateId` or with `step.bridgeUrl`. For eligible lean jobs, `resolveStepTemplate()` first matches a populated live workflow step by `_id` or `uuid`, then queries `findOne()` by the step `_templateId` and job `_environmentId`, then tries `findDeleted()` with the same scope. `isUsableTemplate()` rejects candidates whose type differs from the stored expected type when that type is present. A successful candidate replaces `step.template` in memory and returns `HYDRATED`.

## Resolver hashes route only supported bridge actions

`ExecuteBridgeRequest.execute()` considers the step-resolver path only when `stepResolverHash` is present. It evaluates `IS_STEP_RESOLVER_ENABLED` and `IS_ACTION_STEP_RESOLVER_ENABLED` with `defaultValue: false`; either flag being true enables the path. In that path only `PostActionEnum.EXECUTE` and `PostActionEnum.PREVIEW` are accepted, and other actions throw `BadRequestException`. Without a hash, or when both flags are false, execution falls through to `frameworkRequest.execute()` even if a hash was supplied.

## Local feature flags are parsed from the default value type

`FeatureFlagsService.initialize()` chooses `LaunchDarklyFeatureFlagsService` when `LAUNCH_DARKLY_SDK_KEY` is truthy and otherwise chooses `ProcessEnvFeatureFlagsService`. The latter reads `process.env[context.key]` without renaming the key. Its `getFlag()` returns `defaultValue` for an absent or empty value, converts numeric defaults with `Number(processEnvValue)`, accepts only the exact string `true` as boolean true, and returns raw environment strings for string defaults. Other default-value types fall back to `defaultValue`.

## Failed ClickHouse batches return to the row buffer

`ClickHouseBatchService.flushTable()` swaps `buffer.rows` to a new empty array before inserting the detached batch through `flushBatchWithRetry()`. If insertion still fails after that helper exhausts its configured retries, the catch handler increments `totalFailed` by the batch length, logs the failure, and prepends the failed batch to rows accumulated during the attempt using `[...batchToFlush, ...buffer.rows]`. Its finalizer ends the transaction and resolves the flush promise, so a fulfilled flush attempt does not by itself prove that those rows were inserted.

## Single and batch LRU reads share in-flight fetches

`InMemoryLRUCacheService.get()` and `getMany()` use the same per-store `inflightRequests` map supplied by `getOrCreateStore()`. With caching enabled, single reads can reuse a batch lookup and batch reads can reuse a single lookup for the same effective cache key. Both methods cache fetched values only when they are neither null nor undefined. If `get()` awaits a shared batch promise that resolves to undefined because the batch omitted that key, it falls through to its own `fetchFn()` instead of returning that missing value.

## Workflow payload defaults come from the final step

In the current `VerifyPayload.execute()` implementation, required-variable checks for every workflow step run before default generation. On success, a second loop repeatedly assigns `defaultPayload = verifyPayloadService.fillDefaults(step.template?.variables || [])` and returns the final assignment; it does not merge the per-step objects. Because `VerifyPayloadService.fillDefaults()` creates a fresh payload object on each call, defaults from earlier steps are lost unless they also occur in the final step. A final step with no variables replaces earlier defaults with an empty object.

# Architecture

## System Overview

Novu provides communication infrastructure for products and agents across notification channels.
The dashboard (`apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx`) mounts a React Router application.
Dashboard API helpers and public SDKs send requests to the NestJS API (`apps/api/src/main.ts`).
The API bootstrap configures URI versions, parsing, validation, logging and response handling.
Feature controllers under `apps/api/src/app/` translate requests into typed commands and use-cases.
Internal business services live in `libs/application-generic`; persistence goes through `libs/dal` repositories.
Notification execution runs asynchronously in `apps/worker`, with queue infrastructure shared by backend apps.
`apps/ws` delivers real-time updates using Socket.io and a Redis adapter.
`packages/js` and `packages/react` expose client-side Inbox functionality; `packages/framework` supports code-first workflows.
MongoDB stores application data; Redis supports queues/cache; ClickHouse supports analytics and traces.
Community, Enterprise Cloud and On-Prem Enterprise share this repository with distribution-specific gates.

## Key Components

- **API composition** — `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` assembles feature modules and global guards/interceptors; depends on internal libraries and optional enterprise packages.
- **Dashboard composition** — `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx`, `src/api/` and `src/hooks/` connect routes, permission checks and TanStack Query to backend APIs.
- **Internal layers** — `libs/application-generic` supplies business infrastructure and `libs/dal` supplies repositories; consult their dedicated context for implementation details.
- **Execution and sockets** — `apps/worker` handles background execution; `apps/ws` bridges real-time delivery to Socket.io clients using shared backend infrastructure.
- **Published packages** — `packages/shared`, `framework`, `js` and `react` carry contracts and integrations consumed across apps; changes have a wider build and compatibility surface.

## External Dependencies

- **MongoDB** — primary document persistence, accessed through DAL repositories; schema changes require approval.
- **Redis** — queue, cache and Socket.io infrastructure; host/port configuration must match the service being run.
- **ClickHouse** — analytics, activity and tracing storage; local migrations live under `apps/api/migrations/clickhouse-migrations`.
- **S3 / Azure Blob / GCS** — storage integrations selected by environment; LocalStack provides local S3 emulation.
- **Clerk / Better Auth** — authentication integrations selected by deployment configuration; cloud and self-hosted builds have different wiring.
- **Channel providers** — email, SMS, push and chat integrations; `packages/providers/` is approval-gated.

## What Does NOT Exist Here

- Enterprise implementation is not wholly in the community tree: `enterprise/` wrappers link to the separate `.source` checkout. Do not assume it is available in CE.
- `apps/webhook` is outside active task scope unless a monorepo-wide refactor requires it.
- `libs/internal-sdk` is generated output, not a place for hand-written endpoint fixes.
- `playground/` is demonstration code, not the source of production UI components.

## Better Auth routes are excluded from wildcard CORS

`enableWildcard()` requires `!isBetterAuthRoute(req.url)`, and `isBetterAuthRoute()` matches URLs starting with `/v1/better-auth`. Consequently these routes never qualify for wildcard CORS through this helper, even when the development/other-route condition is true; they use the explicit-origin branch of `corsOptionsDelegate`.

## WebSocket infrastructure must start before listening

## Dashboard agent components

The agents component area composes agent creation dialogs, overview screens, channel selection and provider setup guides, managed-runtime settings, and chat previews. Main entry points include CreateAgentDialog, AgentOverviewTab, AgentSetupSteps, and AgentIntegrationsTab; provider-specific guides and shared setup helpers supply their channel UI. These components connect dashboard pages and environment/auth contexts to the agents and integrations API clients through TanStack Query, use shared provider contracts from @novu/shared, and embed chat functionality from @novu/react.

## Connection badges require a valid positive inbound timestamp

`isAgentIntegrationConnected()` delegates to `hasAgentInboundConnection(connectedAt)`. The helper returns false for a missing value, an invalid date, or a parsed timestamp at or before `0`; it accepts only a valid date with `timestampMs > 0`. Merely linking an integration does not satisfy this dashboard connection predicate.

## Failed email credential saves do not poison the save queue

Inside `useEmailSetupCredentials()`, `saveCredentials()` chains each `updateIntegration()` call onto `saveQueueRef.current`. It returns `next.then(() => undefined)` to preserve rejection for its caller, but stores a separate `next.then(successHandler, failureHandler)` in the queue ref. ## Managed Claude candidates prefer real credentials then descending IDs

`getClaudeManagedAgentIntegrations()` sorts its filtered candidates with `compareClaudeManagedIntegrations()`: entries recognized by `isDemoIntegration()` sort after other entries, and entries in the same demo category use `right._id.localeCompare(left._id)`. `getPreferredClaudeManagedIntegration()` returns element `[0]`, so a real credential is preferred over a demo and the greatest lexicographic `_id` wins within the category. `isDemoIntegration()` includes `AgentRuntimeProviderIdEnum.NovuAnthropic` among its demo providers.

# Conventions

## Naming

- Hygen creates API module files as `<name>.controller.ts` and `<name>.module.ts`, and PascalCase `<Name>Controller` / `<Name>Module` classes.
- Hygen pairs `<name>.usecase.ts` with `<name>.command.ts`; generated classes are `<Name>` and `<Name>Command`, and the use-case entry method is `execute(command)`.
- Protected endpoint method names follow the API rule's `getEntityName`, `listEntityName`, `createEntityName`, `updateEntityName`, `deleteEntityName` convention. Existing legacy names can differ; avoid unrelated renames.
- Tests use `.spec.ts` for API unit specs, `.e2e.ts` for API integration specs, and dashboard Playwright tests under `apps/dashboard/tests/`.
- Biome enforces single-quoted JS/TS strings, double-quoted JSX attributes, semicolons, two-space indentation and a 120-column target.

## Structure

- Work in active apps `api`, `dashboard`, `worker`, `ws`; reuse `packages/shared`, `framework`, `js`, `react`. Do not hand-edit `libs/internal-sdk` or copy UI patterns from `playground/`.
- API controllers handle HTTP contracts; typed commands/use-cases carry business work. Shared business infrastructure belongs in `libs/application-generic`, data access in `libs/dal`.
- API use-cases are registered through feature `usecases/index.ts` and module providers; generators show the expected wiring.
- Dashboard API wrappers belong in `src/api/`, server-state hooks in `src/hooks/`, and reusable UI under `src/components/`; actual primitives are in `src/components/primitives/`.
- Prefer public package entry points: Biome restricts deep `@novu/*` imports. Preserve explicitly documented startup exceptions such as API secrets hydration.
- Ask before adding dependencies, changing MongoDB/ClickHouse schemas or `enterprise/` / `packages/providers/`, or creating UI components outside `apps/dashboard/src/components/`.

## Patterns

- **Controller delegates to a scoped command.** Follow `TenantController`: `usecase.execute(Command.create({ organizationId: user.organizationId, environmentId: user.environmentId, ... }))`. Replace a direct controller database query with a use-case and DAL repository; retain user/environment scope.
- **Protect and describe API contracts.** Use `@RequireAuthentication()` for protected routes, `@ExternalApiAccessible()` for SDK/API-key access and `@OAuthAccessible()` for OAuth access. Document with `@ApiOperation`, response decorators and `@ApiTags`; list APIs use pagination and `@SdkUsePagination`.
- **Keep DTO optionality consistent.** Before: `@ApiProperty() email?: string;`. After: `@ApiPropertyOptional() email?: string;`. Preserve other decorator metadata and check `pnpm check:api-property-optionality` for DTO edits.
- **Use query hooks and invalidate on success.** Follow `useUpdateEnvironment()`: `useMutation({ mutationFn: updateEnvironment, onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [QueryKeys.myEnvironments] }) })`. Replace component-level server-state fetching with the existing API wrapper and query hook.
- **Compose existing form primitives.** `EditEnvironmentSheet` uses `useForm`, a schema resolver, `Form`, `Sheet` and `Button`; show pending/error states and keep field validation with the feature schema.

## Verify Checklist

Before presenting changes, enumerate each applicable result; explain any not applicable item.

- [ ] Scope and approvals: only authorized paths changed; no generated SDK hand edits, new dependencies or unapproved schema/enterprise/provider changes.
- [ ] Architecture: controllers delegate to use-cases; database access uses DAL repositories and preserves organization/environment scope.
- [ ] Contracts: authentication/access decorators, pagination, OpenAPI responses and DTO optionality match the endpoint's intended clients.
- [ ] UI: existing components and TanStack Query are reused; loading/error behavior and relevant query invalidation work.
- [ ] Distribution: CE, Cloud and on-prem EE behavior stays gated appropriately; cloud-only integrations do not become self-hosted requirements.
- [ ] Validation: run the affected project's check/test scripts; API/worker/ws tests use `NODE_ENV=test` and isolated API Mocha specs use `--no-config` when avoiding the destructive harness.
- [ ] Build: run `pnpm build` after package/enterprise changes (also internal library changes per infrastructure guidance); app-only changes do not require a monorepo rebuild.
- [ ] Context: update changed shared knowledge surgically, ground each specific behavior claim to its implementing symbols, and respect the current task's MEX workflow.

## Data access layer

`libs/dal` is the internal `@novu/dal` library for MongoDB persistence. Its public entry point, `libs/dal/src/index.ts`, exposes `DalService`, repository classes, entities, schemas and shared types. `DalService` owns Mongoose connection lifecycle; `BaseRepository` and `BaseRepositoryV2` provide shared persistence operations beneath domain repositories for workflows, subscribers, delivery jobs, integrations and agents. Backend applications and `libs/application-generic` consume this layer for data access beneath their business use-cases.

## Automatic index creation requires an explicit opt-in

`DalService.connect()` sets `autoIndex` from `MONGO_AUTO_CREATE_INDEXES === 'true'`, so an unset variable or any other value disables automatic index creation in its base configuration. It spreads the supplied `config` after `baseConfig`, allowing an explicit `config.autoIndex` to override that environment-derived setting.

## Database destruction is guarded only by test mode

`DalService.destroy()` throws `Error('Allowed only in test mode')` unless `NODE_ENV === 'test'`. When that condition holds it calls `mongoose.connection.dropDatabase()` on the current connection; it does not check the database name or URL before dropping the database.

## Empty context matching includes legacy documents by default

`BaseRepository.buildContextExactMatchQuery()` and `BaseRepositoryV2.buildContextExactMatchQuery()` default to `enabled = true` and `strictEmpty = false`. Undefined or empty `contextKeys` produces `$or` matching either a missing field or `contextKeys: []`; `strictEmpty: true` matches only the empty array. Nonempty keys are copied and sorted, then matched with `$all` plus `$size`, making order irrelevant while requiring the same array length. `enabled: false` returns `{}` without filtering context.

## Transaction fallback depends on which base repository is used

`BaseRepository.withTransaction()` lowercases an error message and reruns `fn(null)` if it contains `replica set` or `transaction`, or if `error.codeName === 'IllegalOperation'`; otherwise it rethrows. `BaseRepositoryV2.withTransaction()` reruns `fn(null)` only when the original message contains the case-sensitive text `Transaction numbers are only allowed on`. Thus the legacy fallback can also catch callback failures whose messages contain `transaction`, and a fallback callback receives no session. Both end the session in `finally`, but only the legacy implementation suppresses `endSession()` rejection.

## Cursor walking preserves caller disjunction filters

Both base repositories use `mergeTopLevelOr()` inside `findWithCursorBasedPagination()` for the page query and the opposite-direction cursor probes. If the caller query already has `$or`, the helper preserves its existing `$and` entries, appends separate `$or` clauses for the caller filter and cursor filter under `$and`, and deletes the top-level `$or`. Without an existing `$or`, it installs the cursor clause directly. Cursor constraints therefore intersect the caller disjunction rather than replacing it.

## Cursor totals cap at fifty thousand independently of the page

`BaseRepository.findWithCursorBasedPagination()` and `BaseRepositoryV2.findWithCursorBasedPagination()` pass the original `query`, without the cursor boundary, to `getCountWithLimit(query, 50001)`. Each helper calls `count()` with `secondaryPreferred` and a `50001` limit. A result equal to `50001` becomes `totalCount: 50000` and `totalCountCapped: true`; a result of exactly `50000` remains uncapped. The reported total describes the original filter, not the number of records remaining after the cursor.

## Array projections explicitly exclude unrequested IDs

`convertSelectToProjection()` converts an array of selected keys into inclusion fields and adds `_id: 0` unless the array explicitly contains `_id`. Object selections are copied as supplied, preserving MongoDB's implicit `_id` inclusion unless the caller sets `_id: 0`; `'*'` returns `undefined` to request no projection. Switching from object syntax to an array can therefore remove `_id` from the result.

## API-key append limits are enforced in the write predicate

`EnvironmentRepository.addApiKey()` includes `apiKeys.${maxKeysCount - 1}: { $exists: false }` in the environment update predicate when `maxKeysCount !== undefined`, alongside the `$push` of the new key. This makes the supplied cap part of the same MongoDB document update rather than a separate count-then-write check. Omitting `maxKeysCount` omits this cap predicate; `matched === 0` returns `null`, covering either a reached cap or an absent environment.

## Single-key deletion requires a second stored key

`EnvironmentRepository.deleteApiKey()` guards its `$pull` update with `'apiKeys.1': { $exists: true }`, so it only attempts deletion when the environment has at least two stored keys at write time. It returns `{ matched, modified }` from `BaseRepository.update()`: `matched === 0` also covers an absent environment, while a matched update with `modified === 0` indicates the supplied `keyQuery` removed nothing. Callers must inspect these counts; this method does not throw for those outcomes.

## Keyed digest event lookup joins through sibling digest transactions

When `digestKey` is truthy, `JobRepository.findDigestEventTriggers()` first finds `StepTypeEnum.DIGEST` jobs whose `digest.digestValue` or legacy `payload.${digestKey}` equals `digestValue`, within the supplied time window, template, environment and subscriber. It deduplicates their `transactionId` values, removes `excludeTransactionIds`, and returns `[]` if none remain. It then selects `JobStatusEnum.COMPLETED` / `StepTypeEnum.TRIGGER` jobs in those transactions with the same scope and window, rather than requiring the trigger job itself to retain the keyed payload.

## Manual middleware owns API body parsing

API `bootstrap()` passes `bodyParser: false` to `NestFactory.create()` because its manual `bodyParser` middleware owns parsing. The documented reason is an instrumented double-parse failure: Nest's parser consumed the stream before the manual parser, causing `stream is not readable`. Preserve this ownership when changing parser registration.

## Generated internal SDK models

The Speakeasy-generated models under `libs/internal-sdk/src/models/` define the internal `@novu/api` SDK contracts. `components/index.ts` exposes DTOs and their wire schemas and JSON helpers; `operations/index.ts` exposes endpoint request and response contracts; `errors/index.ts` exposes transport, API-response and validation errors. The SDK resource classes and request functions under `src/sdk/` and `src/funcs/` consume these contracts when communicating with the API. These files are generated output and must not be hand-edited.

## Fallback error text truncates the body without losing the raw response

`SDKError` limits the body displayed in its message to the first `10000` characters, followed by `...and ${remaining} more chars` when the body is longer. This is a diagnostic display limit: its call to `NovuError` still stores the complete `httpMeta.body` in `body` and the original response in `rawResponse`. Inspect `body` rather than the formatted message when the full error payload is needed.

## Typed API errors take their status from the HTTP response

`ErrorDto` retains the parsed error payload as `data$` but delegates initialization of `statusCode` to `NovuError`, which reads `httpMeta.response.status`. It does not assign `err.statusCode` to the exposed `statusCode` property. If the JSON payload and HTTP status disagree, `error.statusCode` reflects the transport while `error.data$.statusCode` retains the payload value.

## Structured validation messages become a serialized payload fallback

`ValidationErrorDto` uses `err.message` as its Error message only when `typeof err.message === "string"`. An array, object, number, boolean, null or absent message instead produces `API error occurred: ${JSON.stringify(err)}`; arrays are not joined into a friendly sentence. `NovuError` passes that selected text to `Error`, while `ValidationErrorDto` keeps the original payload in `data$` and the field constraint map in `errors`.

## Validation instanceof checks deliberately accept structurally compatible errors

`SDKValidationError[Symbol.hasInstance]` does not check the SDKValidationError prototype. It returns true for any `Error` that has `rawValue`, `rawMessage`, and a callable `pretty` property; the two raw properties are checked for presence, not their value types. `ResponseValidationError` supplies those properties and `pretty()`, so it also satisfies `instanceof SDKValidationError`, preserving the compatibility noted in the implementation. This check cannot distinguish these two error classes.

## Pretty validation diagnostics expand each failed union member

`SDKValidationError.pretty()` and `ResponseValidationError.pretty()` call `formatZodError()` only when `cause instanceof z.ZodError`; otherwise they return `this.toString()`. For Zod issues, `formatZodError()` renders paths from `<root>` and recursively visits every `issue.unionErrors` member for the `invalid_union` code, including numbered member diagnostics. Use `pretty()` to inspect which union alternatives failed rather than relying on the ordinary Error string.

## Subscriber JSON parsing captures syntax failures as validation results

`subscriberGlobalPreferenceDtoFromJSON()` runs both `JSON.parse(x)` and `SubscriberGlobalPreferenceDto$inboundSchema.parse(...)` inside `safeParse()`. The helper catches any exception from that callback, including malformed JSON syntax rather than only Zod failures, and returns `ERR(new SDKValidationError(...))`. `ERR()` produces `{ ok: false, error }`; `SDKValidationError` preserves the original JSON string as `rawValue` and the caught exception as `cause`. Check `ok` before reading the parsed value instead of expecting malformed JSON to throw directly from this helper.

## Novu CLI

`packages/novu` is the published `novu` command-line package. `src/index.ts` registers Connect agent onboarding, app initialization, bridge development and synchronization, translation transfer, and step publishing. Connect coordinates authentication, agent/runtime provisioning, channel setup, and local bridge scaffolding through its pipeline and logging/Ink UI implementations. Dev connects a local framework bridge to the dashboard; Sync and the publishing/translation clients call Novu API endpoints. Templates supply starter applications. Shared contracts come from `@novu/shared`, while generated bridge applications and step handlers integrate with `@novu/framework`.

## Interactive Connect does not select the environment secret key

`resolveConnectAuthMethod()` selects `keyless` first when `options.keyless` is true, then `secret-key-flag` for a nonempty trimmed `options.secretKey`. It selects `secret-key-env` from trimmed `NOVU_SECRET_KEY` only when the session is not interactive. Its interactive test is both `process.stdin.isTTY` and `process.stdout.isTTY` with `CI !== 'true'`; otherwise the fallback is `dashboard-oauth`. `options.ci` is not part of this auth-selection test, so that flag alone does not make an environment key win in a TTY session.

## Connect automatically uses plain logging outside an interactive terminal

`connectCommand()` uses `createLoggingUI()` instead of loading and mounting the Ink UI when `shouldUseLoggingMode()` is true. The predicate is true for `options.ci`, `NOVU_CONNECT_PLAIN` equal to `'1'` or `'true'`, `CI === 'true'`, or either stdin or stdout lacking a TTY. Plain logging therefore does not require explicitly supplying `--ci`.

## Workflow sync also updates agent production bridge URLs on a best-effort basis

After `executeSync()` returns without the `status >= 400` exit branch, `sync()` awaits `syncAgentBridgeUrls()` before returning the workflow sync data. That helper GETs `${bridgeUrl}?action=discover` with `timeout: 5000`, treats missing `agents` as an empty array, and PUTs `{ bridgeUrl }` to `/v1/agents/${encodeURIComponent(agent.agentId)}/bridge`. Updates use `Promise.allSettled()`: individual failures are warnings, and discovery or helper failures are caught and warned. Agent URL failures therefore do not turn an otherwise successful workflow sync into a thrown failure.

## Step publishing rejects production before scaffolding or bundling

`stepPublish()` authenticates, then calls `assertNotProductionEnvironment(envInfo)` before scaffold resolution, discovery, bundling, and the `options.dryRun` branch. `assertNotProductionEnvironment()` calls `process.exit(1)` when `envInfo.type === 'prod'` and instructs the user to promote through the dashboard. Consequently `--dry-run` still requires authentication against a non-production environment; it does not bypass this gate.

## Translation push skips locales absent from organization settings

`pushTranslations()` builds the allowed `targetLocales` from `settings.data.defaultLocale` plus `settings.data.targetLocales`, deduplicated with `Set`. It keeps loaded files only when `targetLocales.includes(file.locale)` and warns for excluded files; if no files remain, it returns without uploading. Failure to fetch organization settings throws `Translations not configured. Please enable translations in your dashboard first.` rather than uploading local files without locale filtering.

## Dev readiness requires health JSON and has no retry-count deadline

`monitorEndpointHealth()` polls `${parsedOptions.origin}${endpointRoute}` until `tunnelHealthCheck()` returns true or `shuttingDown` is set. `tunnelHealthCheck()` appends `?action=health-check`, aborts each request after `5_000` milliseconds, and requires parsed JSON `status === 'ok'`; request or JSON failures return false. The loop waits `1000` milliseconds after an unhealthy result or exception. Reaching counter `10` only changes the spinner help text, so a responding HTTP server alone does not complete readiness and ten attempts are not a startup deadline.

## Shared package contracts and utilities

`packages/shared` supplies the `@novu/shared` contract and utility layer used across the API, dashboard, worker, and internal business libraries. Its main entry point, `src/index.ts`, aggregates DTOs, entity interfaces, types, configuration, provider metadata, and browser-compatible helpers. The package manifest also exposes dedicated subpaths for Node-only outbound network utilities and large provider-override schemas, alongside CommonJS and ESM builds.

## Test and CI dotenv resolution skips generic overrides

`resolveDotenvPath()` treats `NODE_ENV` values `test` and `ci` as isolated: it tries the explicit environment file in `overrideDir`, then that file in `defaultDir`, and never considers the generic `overrideDir/.env`. `getEnvFileNameForNodeEnv()` maps these values to `.env.test` and `.env.ci`; if neither candidate exists the resolver returns `undefined`, even when the generic override exists. The code documents this exclusion as protection against loading developer credentials into database-mutating test runs.

## Channel preferences override workflow-wide enabled defaults

For non-null input, `buildWorkflowPreferences()` merges each channel in this order: `defaultPreferences.channels[channel]`, then `inputPreferences.all.enabled` when it is not `undefined`, then `inputPreferences.channels[channel]`. Thus `all.enabled: false` disables unspecified channels while an explicit channel `enabled: true` still wins; the workflow-wide `readOnly` field is not copied into channels by `defaultChannelPreference`.

## Tag-filter limits count submitted values rather than unique tags

`normalizeTagGroups()` and its object-form helper `normalizeTagGroupsFromObject()` enforce `MAX_TAGS_PER_GROUP = 100` for each OR-group. For `{ and: [{ or: [...] }, ...] }`, the helper additionally enforces `MAX_TAG_GROUPS = 30` and `MAX_TOTAL_TAGS = 200`; the total sums each group's array length without deduplication. `validateOrGroupStrings()` applies the per-group limit to object forms, and limit violations throw `TagsFilterValidationError`.

## Tag query construction requires a match in every OR-group

`buildTagsQuery()` converts one normalized group into `{ tags: { $in: group } }`, but multiple groups into a MongoDB `$and` of those `$in` clauses. A notification must therefore match at least one tag from every group, rather than any tag across all groups. Zero groups produce `{}`, imposing no tag constraint.

## Reply-To token construction silently falls back to the original address

`buildAgentReplyToAddress()` appends `+nv` plus the base36 encoding of a message ObjectId only if `splitAddress()` can split the trimmed base address, `encodeObjectIdBase36()` accepts the message id as exactly 24 hexadecimal characters, and the resulting local-part is at most `MAX_LOCAL_PART_LENGTH = 64` characters. If any check fails, it returns the original `baseAddress` unchanged, including its original whitespace, rather than throwing or truncating the local-part.

## Unsafe override write paths are ignored without mutating the input

`setAtPath()` checks every dotted path segment through `isSafePathSegment()`. An empty segment or any of `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` causes it to return a new shallow `{ ...target }` without applying the supplied value. Callers receive an unchanged copy rather than an exception for these rejected paths.

## Safe JSON serialization distinguishes cycles from shared references

`safeJsonStringify()` tracks the current ancestor stack in its replacer and emits the literal `[Circular]` only when an object reappears on that stack. Reusing the same object in separate non-circular branches is serialized normally, so a repeated reference by itself is not treated as a cycle.

## An invalid in-app target is dropped without discarding a valid URL

`sanitizeInAppRedirect()` returns `undefined` for a missing URL or one rejected by `isValidInAppRedirectUrl()`. ## Method-preserving redirects compare host and port against the initial request

When following a redirect within `maxRedirects`, `safeOutboundRequest()` rejects HTTP `307` or `308` if `nextUrl.host.toLowerCase()` differs from `initialOriginHost`, throwing `SsrfBlockedError` with reason `CROSS_ORIGIN_METHOD_PRESERVING_REDIRECT`. The comparison uses the initial request's URL `host` (hostname and port), not `origin` or the immediately preceding hop; a scheme-only change with the same host string does not trigger this particular rejection.

## Legacy SSRF validation is a cached preflight rather than a guarded request

`validateUrlSsrf()` calls `assertSafeOutboundUrl()` and then `resolvePublicAddresses(parsed.hostname, { useCache: true })`, returning a policy rejection's message or `null` on success. `resolvePublicAddresses()` normally bypasses `DNS_CACHE`, but this explicit flag enables reuse. The legacy helper does not open or pin an HTTP connection and does not inspect subsequent redirects, so its success is not a guarantee about a separate request made afterward.

## JSON-friendly outbound responses can still contain strings

`safeOutboundJsonRequest()` uses `headerString()` to read `content-type` and attempts JSON parsing for values containing `application/json` or `+json`; an empty body in that branch becomes `undefined`. With other content types it attempts parsing only when trimmed text begins with `{` or `[`. A parsing failure leaves the original UTF-8 string, so the generic `<T>` does not ensure that the returned `body` is an object.

## Chat button URL validation accepts leading Liquid before URL parsing

`getChatCardButtonUrlError()` accepts a trimmed value beginning with a complete `{{ ... }}` expression through `isChatCardButtonVariableValue()` and `findLiquidExpressionEnd()`, without validating its remaining text or eventual rendered URL. Otherwise `replaceLiquidExpressions()` substitutes embedded expressions with `novu` before requiring an absolute `http:` or `https:` URL. A bare `payload.url` is plain text and fails that URL check, while `{{ payload.url }}` passes.

## Dashboard pages

The route-level React screens in `apps/dashboard/src/pages/` compose dashboard layouts, feature components, environment/auth context, and API/query hooks. Main entry points include `WorkflowsPage`, `EditWorkflowPage`, `ActivityFeed`, `EnvironmentsPage`, `AgentsPage`, `AgentDetailsPage`, authentication/onboarding pages, and local-bridge pages; `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx` registers routes using `src/utils/routes.ts`. Workflow editing delegates to `components/workflow-editor`, agent screens to `components/agents`, and server communication to dashboard hooks and API helpers.

## Local bridge authentication rejection offers environment selection

When the `getStatelessBridgeStatus()` call in `LocalHandshakePage()` fails, `isBridgeAuthenticationError()` recognizes only a `NovuApiError` with `status === 401` or `rawError.code === BRIDGE_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED_CODE`.
